title: 4th Science Pacing Support
scope: Excerpts only: lesson-content lines ClassThread items cite. No names, rosters, small-group links or student information.
content:
[Nov 30–Dec 4 and Dec 7–11 weekly blocks, Unit 3: Forecasting the Weather] I can use investigations and models to explain how water changes form and travels through the water cycle in different ways. I can gather and analyze weather information to predict weather patterns and explain how weather is different from climate.
[Nov 30–Dec 4 and Dec 7–11 weekly blocks, STEMScopes] 4E3A Properties of Water, 4E3B Water Cycle, 4E4AD Measuring Weather and Climate, and 4E4BC Predicting Weather
[UbD planning document, Unit 3: Forecasting the Weather, Vocabulary] water cycle, evaporation, condensation, precipitation, forecast, front, air mass, meteorologist
[UbD planning document, Unit 3, Understanding] Water continuously cycles between the Earth's surface and atmosphere through evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.
[UbD planning document, Unit 3, Understanding] Meteorologists use collected weather data and technology to predict weather patterns.
[UbD planning document, Unit 3, Acquisition] The stages of the water cycle; how weather data (temperature, wind, precipitation, air pressure) is used to forecast conditions.
